security_audit.summary: Sixteen findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, URLs, and ordinary prose. One medium finding is confirmed: the instructions run Docker Compose from a downloaded third-party checkout, creating container and image supply-chain risk. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The setup instruction launches containers from an external repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed release and image digests, inspect the Compose file, and document required ports, volumes, privileges, and secrets before execution.

content.value_statement: Low average order value limits revenue from every acquired customer. This skill creates ethical upsell sequences with reliable payments, clear offers, and measurable guardrails.
actual_capabilities: Compares pre-purchase order bumps with post-purchase offers.
Designs upsell, optional second offer, downsell, and thank-you paths.
Defines offer copy, pricing, decline, and confirmation requirements.
Identifies stored-payment, merged-order, refund, idempotency, and authentication needs.
Specifies take rate, average order value, refund, conversion, and chargeback metrics.
Outlines a Docker Compose setup path for the referenced self-hosted platform.
limitations: It does not implement application code or configure payment providers automatically.
It does not replace legal, tax, privacy, or card-network compliance review.
Offer and pricing recommendations require controlled testing with sufficient transaction volume.
The referenced deployment depends on an external repository and container images that need independent review.

use_cases.title: Launch a first upsell
use_cases.description: Create a simple complementary offer after payment with an honest decline path and clear order confirmation.

use_cases.title: Specify payment behavior
use_cases.description: Translate the customer flow into requirements for stored credentials, idempotency, refunds, merged orders, and authentication fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Improve funnel economics
use_cases.description: Plan controlled tests that raise average order value while monitoring refunds, chargebacks, and base conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an upsell
prompt_templates.prompt: My product is [product] at [price]. Suggest one complementary post-purchase offer, a fair price, and an honest decline option.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the offer page
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a post-purchase page for [base product] and [upsell]. Include headline, benefit, proof, price, accept text, decline text, and confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Design the decision chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a two-decision flow for [catalog]. Define accept and decline branches, one downsell, stop conditions, and the final thank-you state.

prompt_templates.title: Create a technical specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Write requirements for a one-click upsell using [payment provider] and [store]. Cover credentials, idempotency, authentication, order merging, refunds, events, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Create an upsell for a 49 dollar yoga mat.
output: Offer: Add a carrying strap for 19 dollars.
Accept: Add the strap to my order for 19 dollars.
Decline: No thanks, continue to my order.

output_examples.input: Plan the paths for a coffee subscription upsell.
output: Accept path: Add a grinder, then show the thank-you page.
Decline path: Offer a smaller filter bundle, then end the sequence.
Guardrail: Stop after two decisions and keep every decline clear.

output_examples.input: Define measurements for an existing post-purchase offer.
output: Primary metric: Average order value before and after the launch.
Offer metric: Acceptances divided by views for each offer.
Guardrails: Base conversion, refund rate, and monthly chargeback rate.

best_practices: Use one complementary offer per screen and limit most flows to two decisions.
Make acceptance one tap, keep decline wording honest, and confirm the added charge clearly.
Test one variable at a time while monitoring refunds, chargebacks, and base conversion.
anti_patterns: Do not require customers to re-enter payment details for a one-click offer.
Do not use hidden decline links, guilt-based copy, or false urgency.
Do not launch without testing acceptance, decline, duplicate taps, authentication failure, and refunds.

faq.question: Should I use a pre-purchase bump or post-purchase upsell?
faq.answer: Start post-purchase when protecting base conversion matters. Test a small pre-purchase bump later with conversion as a guardrail.

faq.question: How many offers should the flow contain?
faq.answer: Most funnels should stop after two decisions. Longer chains can increase fatigue, confusion, and support requests.

faq.question: What makes an offer truly one-click?
faq.answer: The platform must reuse a properly stored payment credential without asking the customer to enter card details again.

faq.question: Which metrics should I track?
faq.answer: Track offer take rate, average order value, refunds, base conversion, and chargebacks. Compare results over a meaningful sample.

faq.question: Can the skill deploy the flow for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides design, copy, technical requirements, measurement guidance, and a referenced setup path.

faq.question: How should failed off-session charges be handled?
faq.answer: Show an authentication or recovery step. Never report success when the payment provider declined or requires customer action.
